The Government's case is that the suit land is a fishery, locally known as Magura beel fishery, and it was recorded in the khatian of the Deputy Commissioner under section 20(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as a non-retainable khas land and that the Government has been possessing the same since acquisition. 

 5. The trial Court dismissed the suit after finding, on the basis of the khatian Ext 6, that the plaint's case that Ram Proshad had interest to the extent of 14 annas and odd share in the suit land was altogether baseless; that the plaintiffs had not been able to prove their possession in the suit land; that they brought the suit as a test case by procuring dakhil as Ext. 2 series and kabuliyats which were never tendered to and accepted by the landlord. 

 7. In revision the High Court Division restored the judgment and decree of the trial Court With regard to the plaintiffs' document Ext. 6 which the appellate Court did not at all consider the High. Court Division held that the khatian did not support the plaintiffs case as stated in para 2 of the plaint, that 14 annas 8 gondas and 2 karas and 2 kranti share of the suit land belonged to one Ram Proshad Chakraborty and the remaining 1 anna 1 gonda 1 kara and 1 kranti share belonged to Abdul Wazid and 5 others in khasmaliki right. From Khatian No. 675, filed by the plaintiffs and marked as Ext. 6, the High Court Division held that 120 acres and 40 decimals of land, recorded in that khatian, belonged to Ram Proshad Sarma and Ram Hory Chakraborty in 6-1/3 shares each and the remaining 1/3rd to Gagan Chakraborty, Girish Chakraborty and Norendra Chandra Chakraborty sons of the Gopinath Chabraborty, in equal 1/3rd share. The names of Abdul Wazid and his alleged other co-sharers were nowhere found in that khatian. Suit Plot No. 2934 was found to be recorded as petit land in Ext. 6. 

 8. Mr. Ranadhir Sen, the learned Counsel for the appellants, contend that the trial Court as well as the High Court Division fell in grave error in deciding the question of title of the plaintiffs on the basis of the Khatian Ext 6, wrongly described as the CS Khatian. He has read out several passages from the Introduction to the Assam Land Revenue Manual, Volume I, Fifth Edition, Shillong Printed at the Assam Government Press 1931, in support of his contention that there is no presumption with regard to Ext 6. It is contended that though there had been several experimental surveys in Sylhet area the record of right had never been finally published. The learned Counsel has drawn our attention to the following observation made in the Introduction to the aforesaid Manual: 

 12. The appellants main grievance is that the trial Court and the High Court Division wrongly relied on the khatian Ext. 6. The khatian was the plaintiffs' own document and it is not their case that it is not correct, but they contend that the trial Court and the High Court Division ought to have relied on Wazibul Arz than on Ext. 6. From the report of the local investigation it appears that the thak map of the suit mouza with its Suji and Wajibul Arz were filed by the plaintiffs before the Advocate Commissioner and it was considered in relayment of the suit land, but they were neither exhibited before the trial Court nor they are included in the paper book/additional paper book prepared and placed before us by the appellants for substantiating their title to or possession in the suit land.
